title: Why Specifications Matter
discord:
**Kenapa spec penting untuk AI-assisted development?** :thinking:

Kode saja tidak mendefinisikan sistem. NAEOS menjadikan engineering intent machine-readable: satu spec -> validasi -> artifact -> AI context. Traceable dari awal sampai akhir.

Baca: https://github.com/NAEOS-foundation/naeos
slack:
*Why spec matters*

Code alone does not define a system. NAEOS keeps engineering intent machine-readable: one spec -> validation -> artifacts -> AI context.

https://github.com/NAEOS-foundation/naeos
linkedin:
AI generation is fast. The harder problem is keeping what is built coherent with what was intended.

NAEOS treats engineering intent as a machine-readable model (NEIR). One specification drives normalization, validation, artifact generation, and AI context through a single pipeline — Parser to Governance — so every stage reads the same source of truth.

Explore: github.com/NAEOS-foundation/naeos

title: NEIR: The Engineering Intermediate Representation
discord:
**Apa itu NEIR?** :gear:

NAEOS Engineering Intermediate Representation = satu model terstruktur dari sistem yang sedang dibangun. Semua tool hilir (generator, compiler AI, governance) mengonsumsi konteks engineering yang sama.

Detail: https://github.com/NAEOS-foundation/naeos
slack:
*What is NEIR?*

NEIR is the central engineering model. Downstream tools (generators, AI compiler, governance) all consume the same structured context.

https://github.com/NAEOS-foundation/naeos
linkedin:
NAEOS Engineering Intermediate Representation (NEIR) is the model at the center of the pipeline.

Instead of scattered docs, prompts, and tickets, there is one structured model of the system being built. Validators, generators, the AI compiler, and governance all consume the same context — so downstream checks and outputs cannot silently disagree with the architecture.

title: Governance: Policies and Audit Trails
discord:
**Siapa yang memverifikasi kode hasil AI?** :shield:

NAEOS menyediakan governance: policy, artifact review, audit trail, dan verifikasi. Cocok untuk organisasi yang butuh kontrol engineering.

Detail: https://github.com/NAEOS-foundation/naeos
linkedin:
We shipped a control plane for agent-driven engineering in v3.6.0 — and it is fully testable in the open repo.

What the code actually does:
- Policy evaluation over spec context (gt, lt, exists, not_empty)
- Fail-closed execution gate: allow / deny / require-approval, deny always wins
- Artifact review that flags TODO markers, placeholders, and missing license headers
- A tamper-evident decision ledger with evidence filters

No demos. No screenshots. Code, tests, and docs in the repository.

Review: github.com/NAEOS-foundation/naeos

title: Security Fix: We Closed Our Own CRITICAL Bypass
discord:
**Demo dalam dua bahasa.** :earth_asia:

Video demo NAEOS tersedia EN dan ID.

English: https://naeos.dev/download/
Bahasa Indonesia: https://naeos.dev/id/download/
slack:
*Demo in two languages.*

English: https://naeos.dev/download/
Bahasa Indonesia: https://naeos.dev/id/download/
linkedin:
Today we closed a CRITICAL gap in our own guardrails — in public.

We built an adversarial harness that attacks NAEOS' governance like an attacker would: 17 scenarios across policy evaluation, the control plane, artifact review, the prompt layer, and the pipeline. It found 12 ways rules could be bypassed. One was CRITICAL — a prompt override file could silently strip policy guidance from generated AGENTS.md.

That bypass is closed on main today (PR #154): overrides that drop governed files or remove policy markers are rejected at load. No secrets, no hidden roadmaps — the remaining findings are public issues: #145-#152.

Dogfooding means breaking your own platform before anyone else does.
